resources.string: Telemetry and control for your ESP32 projects
Common questions for Home and Catalog. Tap a topic to expand the answer.
ESP32 does not appear when scanning

Power on the ESP32 and press RESET. In Arduino IDE, open Serial Monitor at 115200 baud and confirm the firmware ready banner. From a module, open Bluetooth, tap refresh to scan, move closer, and stop scanning when your board appears under Scanned Devices.

Open the module from Catalog, then use its Bluetooth button to scan and connect. If the board was paired before, try Paired Devices. If it still fails, forget the device in Android Bluetooth settings, scan again, and pair from Scanned Devices. Match Classic/BLE and Simple/Binary to your sketch.

Home shows the last session status. Open Catalog, enter a module, and connect Bluetooth there. Only one phone should control the ESP32 at a time — close other apps using the link. When connected, Home updates to Connected and the hologram opens that recent module.
Module controls or telemetry do nothing

Connect Bluetooth inside the module first. Confirm matching firmware and protocol in module settings (Classic Simple, Classic Binary, BLE Binary, or SoftAP where supported). Stay on the live screen while testing. Reflash the matching sketch from Codes and Documents if the Serial Monitor never shows a ready banner.
First-time setup — where do I start?

Tap Catalog on Home. Open Control panel (free) or another module, then Codes for the ESP32 ZIP and docs. Upload the sketch in Arduino IDE, connect Bluetooth from the module toolbar, and use module settings to match the protocol. Tap the hologram later to reopen your last module.
How do I open modules from Home?

Use the Catalog button to browse all modules. Tap a card to open an unlocked module, or expand the hologram thumbnail for details. Tap the center hologram on Home to reopen the last module you used. About this App is under the Catalog button (or beside it in landscape).
How do Pro modules and the sparkle work?

PRO modules need a subscription, coins, or an unlock grant. Tap the gold PRO badge to open subscription options, or expand a locked card for coin unlock. The sparkle is an occasional explorer gift: watch an ad for a short Pro trial. When a Pro module is enabled it keeps the PRO badge and shows a pulsing green border; the sparkle hides until the gift is available again.

Match the blue numbered badges on the Home screen image (1–6) to the items below.

1. Quick Start (bottom): reconnects to the last saved Bluetooth device, or sends you to scan for a new device.

2. Catalog: opens the module catalog (Control panel, Smart home, and more). Tap a module to open it.

3. Bluetooth: opens the device list to scan, connect, and check the current connection status.

4. Codes and Documents: opens PDF guides and lets you share or save the ESP32_BT_Controller-main.zip code file.

5. Tutorial: opens this step-by-step app guide.

6. Help (top-right): shortcut for quick troubleshooting tips.

This video shows how to prepare the ESP32 in Arduino IDE:

- Open ESP32_BT_Controller.ino in Arduino IDE (download the ZIP from the app in step 2 if you do not have the sketch yet).

- Select the correct ESP32 board under Tools > Board.

- Select the serial port connected to your ESP32 under Tools > Port.

- Upload the sketch to the ESP32.

- Open Tools > Serial Monitor and set the baud rate to 115200.

- Press the ESP32 RESET button.

- Confirm the monitor prints: ESP32 Bluetooth Receiver Ready.

- When you see that message, the ESP32 is waiting for a Bluetooth connection from the app (step 4).

This video shows how to get the project files from the app:

- Open Codes and Documents on the Home screen and tap the ESP32 BT Controller ZIP item.

- Choose Share or send to email or messaging, or Save to Downloads to keep a copy on the phone.

- Open the ZIP where you saved it or from the app you shared to.

- Extract the archive if needed and locate ESP32_BT_Controller.ino.

- Transfer the folder to your computer if you uploaded from the phone, then continue with step 3 in Arduino IDE.
Connect to the ESP32 with Bluetooth

This GIF shows how to connect the app to the ESP32-BT device:

- From the Home screen, tap the Bluetooth button.

- On the Bluetooth screen, tap the refresh icon in the top app bar to start scanning.

- When ESP32-BT appears, tap the X icon to stop scanning.

- Check the Scanned Devices list and find ESP32-BT.

- If this is the first connection, tap ESP32-BT from Scanned Devices to pair and connect.

- If the ESP32 was already paired before, tap ESP32-BT from Paired Devices to connect faster.

- After the connection succeeds, the app returns to the Home screen.

- Confirm that the Bluetooth button now shows the Connected status.

This video shows how to review and apply the controller settings:

- From the Home screen (Bluetooth Connected), tap Catalog.

- Open Control panel, then tap the settings icon in the top bar to open Control panel settings.

- On RC Controller Settings, review Joystick Settings and choose the behavior for the left and right sticks.

- Review Initial Switch Positions and set the starting state for switches S1 to S6.

- Review Initial Knob Values and set the starting value for the left and right knobs.

- Return to the Home screen after the configuration is saved.

- Tap Catalog again, then tap Control panel to open the controller.

- Confirm that joystick behavior, switch states, and knob values are applied correctly on the RC screen.

The RC Control screen runs in landscape. The numbers on the image match this list:

1. Header indicators — Left: analog gauge with integer value and title from ESP32 telemetry. Right: battery-style level and title from telemetry. Both update when the firmware sends new indicator data.

2. Seven-segment displays — Left and right numeric panels (for example RPM). Each has its own title, color, and on/off state from firmware telemetry.

3. Status LEDs — Four LEDs on each side (eight total). Left uses the lower four bits of the LED byte; right uses the upper four. Each LED lights when its bit is set in incoming telemetry.

4. Joysticks — Left and right 3D sticks. Drag to send X and Y in the control packet. Return behavior (spring, hold, etc.) is set per side under Joystick Settings in RC Controller Settings.

5. Switches (S1–S6) — Three toggles on the left (S1–S3) and three on the right (S4–S6). Each maps to a bit in the switch byte; initial on/off states are configured in settings.

6. Rotary knobs — Left and right knobs. Turn to set a 0–100% style auxiliary value sent continuously to the ESP32.

7. Action buttons — Four momentary buttons (upper and lower on each side). Press to send one-shot event packets: CENTER_TOP_LEFT, CENTER_BOTTOM_LEFT, CENTER_TOP_RIGHT, and CENTER_BOTTOM_RIGHT.

8. Center telemetry plot — Live graph area fed by Bluetooth plot series from the ESP32.

While this screen is open, control packets are sent continuously. Connect over Bluetooth before opening RC Control so telemetry and inputs stay in sync with the ESP32.

This video tests every RC screen component from step 6 while the Arduino IDE Serial Monitor runs at 115200 baud next to the app.

Bench debug is the same for Classic Simple, Classic Binary, and BLE Binary (match Connection type in RC Settings to your sketch):

- Firmware default is simulate mode: sticks/knobs/switches on the phone are echoed into panel, indicator, LED, and plot telemetry (no extra wiring).

- Set `TELECON_DEBUG` / `TELECON_SERIAL_INJECT` to 1 (or Classic Binary equivalent) and open Serial Monitor at 115200.

- Connect over Bluetooth, open RC Control, complete handshake (`RC:ACK`).

What the video should show (same order as step 6):

1. Header indicators — Move left/right knobs; analog and battery gauges follow. Serial may log TX telemetry.

2. Seven-segment displays — Move left/right sticks; panel numbers follow stick X (or your firmware mapping).

3. Status LEDs — Toggle switches; LED bits follow the switch byte.

4. Joysticks — Move left then right sticks; Serial shows RX control (text `RC:CTRL` or binary `AA 55`).

5. Switches (S1–S6) — Toggle each switch; confirm RX switch bits and LED feedback.

6. Rotary knobs — Turn both knobs; confirm RX knob values and gauge feedback.

7. Action buttons — Press each side button; Serial shows `RC:BTN` or `BB 66` event.

8. Center plot — Move sticks/knobs; four plot traces update. Labels come from RC Settings → Plot labels.

Optional: type a protocol line in Serial Monitor (`TELECON_SERIAL_INJECT`) to inject telemetry toward the phone (same idea on Classic and BLE).

When finished, center sticks and return controls to a safe default before driving real hardware (`TELECON_USE_HW_IO 1`).

This video shows how to drive the left and right seven-segment displays on the RC screen (step 6, item 2).

Bench setup (same for Classic Simple, Classic Binary, and BLE Binary):

- Flash the matching Control Panel sketch with simulate / echo mode (`TELECON_USE_HW_IO 0` on BLE; Classic Simple auto-echo; Classic Binary after the unified debug update).

- In RC Settings, select the connection mode that matches the sketch, then connect and open RC Control.

- Open Serial Monitor at 115200 if you want TX/RX logs.

What the video should show:

- Move the left stick — left panel value tracks the mapping (typically stick X → 0–9999).

- Move the right stick — right panel updates the same way.

- Optional Serial inject (when `TELECON_SERIAL_INJECT` is 1):
 Classic Simple: `RC:DATA,left,100,right,200,lo,1,ro,1,lg,1,rg,1,analog,42,batt,88,led,0F`
 Classic/BLE Binary: use firmware inject helpers or stick echo (binary `CC 11` is sent automatically).

If panels do not update, verify handshake ACK, connection mode matches the sketch, and RC Control is open.
Test analog, battery, and LED telemetry

This video shows how to test the left analog indicator, right battery indicator, and status LEDs on the RC screen (step 6, items 1 and 3).

Bench setup (same for Classic Simple, Classic Binary, and BLE Binary):

- Use simulate / echo firmware (sticks and knobs feed gauges; switch byte feeds LEDs).

- Match Connection type in RC Settings to the sketch, connect, open RC Control.

What the video should show:

- Turn the left knob — left analog gauge follows (0–255 mapping).

- Turn the right knob — battery indicator follows.

- Toggle switches — status LEDs follow the switch bitfield.

- Optional Serial inject of `RC:DATA,...,analog,75,batt,90,led,0F` on Classic Simple, or rely on binary `CC 22` echo on Classic/BLE Binary.

If nothing updates, verify Bluetooth handshake, mode match, and that simulate mode is enabled (not HW-only with no sensors).

This video shows how plot channel labels are set in the app and how four live plot channels drive the center graph on the RC screen (step 6, item 8).

Part 1 — Plot labels in RC Controller Settings:

- Open RC Controller Settings.

- Set Plot 1–4 (for example "Volts", "Amps", "RPMs", "Temp"). Firmware no longer sends `RC:PLOTCFG` / `CC 44` names.

Part 2 — Bench plot values (same for Classic Simple, Classic Binary, and BLE Binary):

- Use simulate / echo firmware: plot channels map from knobs/sticks (typically lk, lx, rk, ry → v0…v3 / four `CC 33` bytes).

- Match Connection type to the sketch, connect, open RC Control so the dual-pane graph is visible.

- Move knobs and sticks — all four traces should update.

- Optional Serial inject on Classic Simple: `RC:PLOT,v0,120,v1,80,v2,200,v3,40`

If labels are wrong, edit Plot labels in settings. If the graph stays flat, verify handshake, mode match, and simulate/echo mode.
Telemetry and control for ESP32 over Bluetooth
TeleCon4ESP32 connects your phone to ESP32 hardware over Bluetooth. Control sticks, switches, knobs, and view live telemetry from your firmware.
How we handle Bluetooth, local settings, and ads

Bluetooth: device discovery, pairing, and live control/telemetry with hardware you connect — not sent to MICSBOL servers.

Local storage: last device and RC settings on your phone only.

Ads: Google AdMob may collect advertising identifiers and usage data. See the Privacy Policy for details and Google ad settings.

Each card on the Greenhouse screen maps to Bluetooth telemetry (GH:DATA) or commands (GH:SET). Wire your ESP32 firmware to match these keys.

I2C SDA=21, SCL=22 → BME280 (climate) + BH1750 (lux)
GPIO 4 → DS18B20 outside temperature
GPIO 34 → soil moisture (analog)
GPIO 27/33 → tank ultrasonic (trig/echo)
GPIO 13 → fan relay | 14 → heater | 16 → pump
GPIO 17 → grow lights | 19 → vent servo PWM
GPIO 32 → flow sensor pulse (optional)

ESP32-CAM (separate board): live video over Wi‑Fi at http://192.168.4.1
CAM gimbal (free pins): GPIO 13 → pan servo | GPIO 12 → tilt servo
(GH:SET cam_pan / cam_tilt, 0–100, 50 = center)
Shows Bluetooth link, Auto/Manual mode, device name, and time since the last GH:DATA line.
GH:DATA,auto,1,device,ESP32-GH01\nOnline = Bluetooth connected. Updated time = last GH:DATA received.
Main inside temperature, humidity, VPD, and stability badge. VPD is vapor pressure deficit (kPa).
GH:DATA,temp,26.2,hum,68,vpd,1.1,stable,1\nBME280 on I2C (pins 21/22). ESP32 may compute vpd from temp+hum.
Soil moisture percent and optional target band shown under the value.
GH:SET,soil_min,40,soil_max,55\nOptional — set moisture targets stored in ESP32 NVS.
Ambient light in lux and grow-light relay state.
GH:DATA,light,12400,lights,0\nBH1750 on I2C; lights = relay feedback on GPIO 17.
Temperature difference inside vs outside and roof vent opening percent.
GH:DATA,temp_out,23.0,vent,40\nOr send delta directly: GH:DATA,delta,3.2\nOutside: DS18B20 on GPIO 4. Vent: servo on GPIO 19.
Water reservoir level and time since last irrigation cycle.
GH:DATA,tank,78,last_irr,360\nUltrasonic on GPIO 27/33. last_irr = minutes since last pump run.
Temperature, humidity, and VPD history. Uses demo data until the ESP32 sends history arrays.
GH:DATA,hist_temp,18|19|20,hist_hum,72|74,hist_vpd,0.4|0.35\nPipe-separated floats logged every 15 min on ESP32.
Fan, heater, pump, and grow lights. Sliders set vent opening and climate targets.
On the live camera screen, drag the aim pad to move the ESP32-CAM pan/tilt gimbal. Center resets both axes to 50.
GH:SET,cam_pan,50,cam_tilt,50\n0–100 each; 50 = center. CAM pins: pan GPIO 13, tilt GPIO 12.
When Auto is on, the ESP32 runs climate rules using target_temp and target_hum. Manual mode keeps app buttons in control.
Screen components, WT protocol, and ESP32 wiring

This dashboard reads WT:DATA lines over Bluetooth SPP. Ultrasonic or analog level sensors report fill percent, volume, pump state, and alert thresholds. Store level history in NVS or SPIFFS for the chart.
Shows the screen title, device name, refresh action, and an ESP32 Connected badge when Bluetooth SPP is active.
WT:DATA,level,74,cap,500,pump,0,status,0,device,ESP32-WT01\nConnection badge follows Bluetooth link state; no separate GPIO required beyond the status LED on GPIO 2.
3D tank visualization with animated fill percent, volume/capacity readout, and a progress bar. Level is computed from the ultrasonic or analog sensor.
WT:DATA,level,74,cap,500\nlevel: 0–100 percent full. cap: tank capacity in liters (stored in NVS, sent on connect and when changed).
Metric chips — volume, capacity, last updated
Three quick-read chips below the level card. Volume is derived from level × capacity; last updated shows seconds since the last WT:DATA line.
WT:DATA,level,74,cap,500\nApp computes volume = cap × level / 100. Optional: send updated_ago,2 or last_time,10:30 in WT:DATA for explicit timestamps.
Status badge shows Normal, Low, or Critical based on firmware thresholds or float switches. Pump badge reflects relay output state.
WT:DATA,pump,0,status,0\nstatus: 0=normal, 1=low, 2=critical. pump: 0=off, 1=on. Firmware may set status from level thresholds or GPIO 35/36 float switches.
Switches the level history chart between 24-hour, 7-day, and 30-day views. The ESP32 should store separate buffers per period in NVS.
WT:DATA,period,7,hist_level,72|71|70|69|68|67|66\nperiod: 1=24H, 7=7D, 30=30D. hist_level = pipe-separated percent samples for the active period.
Area chart of tank fill percent with average, minimum, and maximum stats for the selected period. Grid lines mark 0–100% on the Y axis.
Bottom row with online/offline dot and last updated clock time. Goes offline if no WT:DATA received within the heartbeat timeout (default 10 s).
WT:DATA,level,74,online,1,last_time,10:30\nonline: 1=sensor responding, 0=timeout. Omit keys to let the app infer from message arrival.
Toggle the fill pump relay from the app. The ESP32 confirms the new state in the next WT:DATA line.
WT:DATA confirms pump state after each WT:SET.
GPIO assignments for every element on the Water Tank dashboard. Ultrasonic echo must use a 3.3 V-safe divider; relay outputs are active-high.
Send WT:DATA every 1–2 s for live level and pump state; hist_level and stats every 30–60 s.

This dashboard reads SH:DATA lines over Bluetooth SPP (no camera). Aggregate room device states, climate sensors, energy metering, security contacts, and water usage from relays, DHT sensors, INA219, door/window reed switches, and flow meters. Store event logs in NVS or SPIFFS.
Top bar — connection and system status
Shows Online/Offline from Bluetooth + last SH:DATA, device id, update age, and an “All Systems Normal” badge when status=0 and no open contacts.
SH:DATA,status,0,device,ESP32-SH01\nstatus: 0 = all normal, 1 = warning (open door/window or fault).
Horizontal cards with a room photo, active device count, and controllable device icons (relays/lock). Sensors (thermostat, motion) are display-only.

SH:DATA,living_light,1,living_ambience,1,living_outlet,0,living_on,2,living_total,3,living_temp,21,living_alert,window,kitchen_light,1,kitchen_appliance,0,kitchen_water,0,kitchen_on,1,kitchen_total,3,kitchen_temp,23,bedroom_light,0,bedroom_on,0,bedroom_total,1,bedroom_temp,19,garage_light,1,garage_lock,0,garage_on,1,garage_total,2,garage_temp,18,garage_alert,door\nalert values: omit key or none, window, door.
Quick-glance tiles for HVAC comfort, live home power draw, security lock state, and daily water consumption.
Area chart of home power draw (kW) over the day. The highlighted dot marks the current reading; axis labels show time blocks from midnight to midnight.
SH:DATA,power_kw,1.8,hist_power,0.4|0.3|0.6|1.2|2.4|2.1|1.8|1.5|1.0|0.5\nhist_power = hourly kW samples (pipe-separated). Send power_kw every 1–2 s; history every 30–60 s.
Chronological log of automation triggers: locks, lights, motion, windows, and water usage. Newest events appear at the top.
SH:DATA,event0,door_locked|09:30,event1,light_on|09:15,event2,motion|08:47\nOr event0,door_locked,event0_t,09:30. Codes: door_locked, light_on, motion, windows, water.
Toggle relays or smart plugs per room and device. Scenes turn lights off or arm Away (lights/outlets off, garage lock on). Request a full telemetry refresh after wiring changes.
SH:DATA confirms state after each SH:SET.
GPIO assignments for the DIY DevKit hub (no camera). Relay outputs are active-high; reed switches and PIR use INPUT_PULLUP. Climate tile averages DHT22 on GPIO 4/5/12.
Send SH:DATA every 1–2 s for live watts and temperatures; room counters and event logs every 30–60 s.
Unable to reach the ESP32 doorbell camera. Check WiFi and device power.

DIY ESP32 smart door lock intercom

This dashboard combines a Wi-Fi video feed from an ESP32-CAM doorbell with Bluetooth SPP lock control. Read DL:DATA lines for door state, relay position, and signal strength. Send DL:SET commands to unlock, lock, or pulse the strike relay on GPIO 12 (active LOW).
Top bar — title, connection, and call timer
Shows the Front Door title, ESP32 connection badge, elapsed call duration, help shortcut, and application settings. Connection follows camera stream or DL:DATA heartbeat.
DL:DATA,device,ESP32-DL01,online,1,call,65\nonline: 1 = SPP connected and firmware responding; GPIO 2 status LED mirrors link state. call: elapsed seconds since session start.
Status card — live video and badges
Large green card with Wi-Fi signal strength, ESP32 online chip, live MJPEG video from the doorbell camera, door lock/unlock badge, and ESP32 status overlay on the feed.

DL:DATA,lock,1,relay,LOW,sig,-42,door,0\nlock: 0=unlocked, 1=locked. relay: LOW/HIGH mirrors GPIO 12. sig: Wi-Fi RSSI in dBm. door: 0=open, 1=closed (GPIO 14 reed). Video: HTTP MJPEG at http://192.168.4.1/stream.
Drag the white lock thumb to the right to send an unlock command. Disabled when the ESP32 is offline. Snaps back after release unless dragged past 85% of the track.
DL:DATA confirms lock,0 and relay,LOW after a successful unlock.
Quick action cards — Send Key and Send Code
Two side-by-side cards for instant unlock (Send Key) and lock (Send Code) signals. Both drive GPIO 12; unlock pulls active LOW, lock releases to HIGH.
DL:DATA,lock,0,relay,LOW after unlock. DL:DATA,lock,1,relay,HIGH after lock.
Floating pill bar toggling two-way audio and the live camera stream. Mic and speaker use I2S on GPIO 4/25; camera streams over Wi-Fi from the ESP32-CAM module.
DL:DATA,mic,1,spk,1,cam,1\nmic/spk/cam: 0=off, 1=on. Firmware enables I2S paths and camera HTTP server accordingly.
Relay panel — GPIO 12 state and pulse
Glass card showing relay PIN 12 state (LOW/HIGH) with active-LOW wiring note. Trigger 2s Pulse momentarily energizes the strike for 2 seconds then returns to locked/HIGH.
DL:SET,pulse,1\nHolds GPIO 12 LOW for 2000 ms then sets HIGH.
Ends the intercom session, stops the camera stream, resets the call timer, and navigates back. Does not change the physical lock state.
DL:SET,call,0\nOptional: firmware may disable I2S and camera server when call ends. App stops MJPEG locally regardless.
GPIO assignments for every element on the Smart Door Lock dashboard. GPIO 12 lock relay is active LOW; use a flyback diode on inductive loads.
Send DL:DATA every 1–2 s for lock/relay state; Wi-Fi signal and door reed every 5–10 s. Pulse command holds GPIO 12 LOW for 2 s.

This dashboard reads SL:DATA lines over Bluetooth SPP. Control relays and PWM dimmers for bulbs and LED strips, read online/signal status per zone, and apply automation rules (motion, away, sunset). Store device names and schedules in NVS.
Shows the Smart Lighting title, back action, help shortcut, and application settings. Bluetooth link state is inferred from incoming SL:DATA lines.
SL:DATA,device,ESP32-SL01,online,1\nonline: 1 = SPP connected and firmware responding; GPIO 2 status LED mirrors link state.
Room preview with hotspot markers and a count of lights currently on versus total registered devices. Updates whenever any zone state changes.
SL:DATA,on_count,7,total,12,living,1,kitchen,1,bedroom_lamp,0\non_count and total are computed by firmware from relay/PWM states; individual keys mirror device card toggles.
Master control that switches every registered light zone at once. Uses GPIO 4 master relay bus or broadcasts SL:SET to all channels.
SL:DATA confirms all zone states after SL:SET,all,1 or SL:SET,all,0.
Each card shows a room thumbnail, device name, type, online badge, Wi-Fi signal percent, and on/off state. Tap a card to toggle that zone.

SL:DATA,living,1,kitchen,1,bedroom_lamp,0,bedroom_ceiling,1,bedroom_closet,0,hallway,1,dining,0,staircase,1,bathroom,1,office,0,garage,1,patio,0,sig_living,98,sig_kitchen,92\nZone keys: 0=off, 1=on. Optional sig_* keys: 0–100 link quality for BLE mesh nodes.
Pair a smart bulb over Bluetooth or scan a QR code to register an LED strip controller. New zones are stored in NVS and appear in the matching section.
SL:DATA,pair_state,0,devices,12\npair_state: 0=idle, 1=discovering, 2=paired. Hold GPIO 5 to enter pairing mode on the ESP32.
Toggle auto-off when away, motion-activated lighting, and sunset sync. Motion uses GPIO 32 PIR; sunset uses GPIO 34 LDR or NTP time from Wi-Fi.
SL:DATA,auto_away,1,motion,1,sunset,1\nauto_away: turn all off when no motion for 30 min. motion: turn on hallway/staircase on PIR. sunset: dim warm zones at civil dusk.
GPIO assignments for every element on the Smart Lighting dashboard. PWM outputs drive MOSFET dimmers; relay outputs are active-high.
Send SL:DATA every 1–2 s for live zone states; on_count and signal keys every 10–30 s.

This dashboard reads SP:DATA lines over Bluetooth SPP. Use an INA219 or ACS712 for current, a voltage divider for bus voltage, and pulse counting or inverter UART for kWh totals. Store daily/monthly counters in NVS.
Top bar — connection and grid mode
Shows Bluetooth link, active/waiting/offline state, grid export/import, device ID, panel name, and time since the last SP:DATA line.
SP:DATA,device,ESP32-SP01,panel_name,LinCore,grid_mode,1,status,0\nOnline = SP:DATA received while Bluetooth is connected.
Background tint follows live solar_w: dawn tones at low output, bright gold at peak production. Driven by solar_w and max_solar_w from telemetry.
SP:DATA,solar_w,480,max_solar_w,1200\nMap your array peak watts to max_solar_w so the UI scales correctly.
Battery SOC badge, panel illustration, and cumulative generation for today, this month, and all time.
SP:DATA,batt_pct,89,today_kwh,725,month_kwh,523,total_kwh,1800\nReset today_kwh at midnight in ESP32 NVS.

Bidirectional bar chart: blue bars above the baseline show produced energy; purple bars below show consumed energy. Week view groups three sub-daily bars under each day (Mon–Sun). Today view uses eight 3-hour blocks (00:00–21:00) with three hourly bars each. The tallest bar in each group is highlighted; faded bars are lower intervals.

SP:DATA,cons_week_kwh,472,cons_day_kwh,68,prod_kwh,492,export_kwh,183,batt_used_kwh,72,hist_prod,6|14|9|8|18|11,hist_cons,12|7|9|14|8|11\nhist_prod = produced kWh per sub-interval (21 for week, 24 for day). hist_cons = consumed kWh (or sum hist_cons_home|batt|grid). Send 7 daily totals and the app expands to 3 sub-bars per day. SP:SET,period,1 (today, 8×3h blocks) or 7 (week).
Battery capacity, estimated time to full charge, total energy charged, and live bus voltage/current/grid watts.
Instantaneous watts for solar production, home load, battery charge/discharge, and grid import/export.
SP:DATA,solar_w,480,load_w,310,batt_w,170,grid_w,120\nbatt_w positive = charging. grid_w positive = export, negative = import.
Inverter on/off switch, grid mode, panel efficiency, fault code, energy split (home/battery/grid), and daily counter reset.

I2C INA219 (solar current): SDA GPIO 21, SCL GPIO 22
Load CT (ACS712): GPIO 34 (ADC)
Battery shunt (INA219 #2): I2C address 0x41
Voltage divider (24 V bus): GPIO 35 (ADC, 100k/10k)
Inverter enable relay: GPIO 26
Status LED: GPIO 2
Send SP:DATA every 500 ms for watts; counters every 30–60 s.
